US Imposes Tariffs on Romanian Medical Devices, Industry Faces Mounting Pressure

The United States has imposed a 25% tariff on medical equipment and devices imported from Romania, a measure that has sent ripples through Romania’s domestic industry. The trade policy, which came into effect earlier this month, directly targets a broad range of products including diagnostic imaging devices, surgical instruments, and patient monitoring systems manufactured in Romania.

Industry representatives report that the sudden tariff has already resulted in significant disruption. “Exports to the US accounted for nearly 18% of our annual sales,” said Andrei Vasilescu, spokesperson for the Romanian Association of Medical Devices Producers. “With these tariffs, our competitiveness has been sharply reduced overnight.”

Several companies have reported holding back shipments originally scheduled for US clients, and some production facilities in Bucharest and Cluj have reduced operating shifts in response to anticipated lower demand. “We had to place over 80 employees at our Timișoara site on temporary leave,” confirmed Elena Dumitru, HR director at Meditech Solutions, one of the country’s leading device manufacturers. “We are reviewing our staffing levels weekly as the situation continues to evolve.”

Analysts project that if the tariffs remain in place, smaller firms could be forced to consolidate or scale down operations. “The current environment is deeply uncertain,” said Daniel Iliescu, a trade policy analyst at MarketView Romania. “Firms are reassessing their export strategies and some are considering shifting focus to EU markets.”

The government has stated that it is seeking dialogue with US trade officials. Meanwhile, industry stakeholders warn that prolonged trade barriers could hamper investment and threaten the stability of the medical equipment and devices sector in Romania.
